name: BST Ordering Basics
description: A binary search tree keeps smaller values on the left and larger values on the right, letting comparisons prune the search space.
exampleJava: if (target < root.val) root = root.left; else root = root.right;
commonMistakes: Traversing both subtrees like a general binary tree
Forgetting that inorder traversal of a BST is sorted

name: BST Search
description: Use comparisons to move only one step down the tree at a time instead of scanning the whole structure.
exampleJava: while (root != null && root.val != target) root = target < root.val ? root.left : root.right;
commonMistakes: Searching both children recursively
Moving in the wrong direction after a comparison

name: BST Inorder Is Sorted
description: An inorder traversal visits BST values in ascending order, which powers validation and order-statistics reasoning.
commonMistakes: Treating preorder or level order as sorted
Not connecting inorder ordering back to the BST property

name: BST Validation by Range
description: A valid BST must satisfy global low and high bounds, not just local parent-child comparisons.
exampleJava: return low < root.val && root.val < high && valid(root.left, low, root.val) && valid(root.right, root.val, high);
commonMistakes: Checking only immediate children
Forgetting that an entire subtree inherits ancestor bounds

name: BST Insert
description: Insert by descending left or right until the correct null child position is found.
commonMistakes: Losing the returned child link during recursion
Inserting on the wrong side and breaking ordering

name: LCA in BST
description: The BST property lets you stop when the two targets split to different sides of the current node.
exampleJava: if (p < root.val && q < root.val) root = root.left;
commonMistakes: Using full binary-tree LCA logic when simple direction checks are enough
Not handling the case where one target is the current node

name: Kth Smallest by Inorder
description: Because inorder is sorted, the kth visited node is the kth smallest value.
commonMistakes: Sorting values after collecting them when a single inorder pass is enough
Counting nodes in preorder instead of inorder

name: Successor and Neighbor Reasoning
description: Track the best larger candidate while moving through the BST to find successor-like answers.
exampleJava: if (target < root.val) { successor = root.val; root = root.left; } else root = root.right;
commonMistakes: Returning the parent blindly
Ignoring better candidates discovered on the way down

name: BST Range Pruning
description: Skip whole subtrees when the current value proves they cannot contribute to the answer.
exampleJava: if (root.val < low) return dfs(root.right, low, high);
commonMistakes: Traversing both subtrees even when one side is impossible
Forgetting to keep valid middle nodes in the answer

name: BST Delete and Restructure
description: Deletion must preserve ordering across the zero-child, one-child, and two-child cases.
commonMistakes: Dropping a subtree while reconnecting children
Copying the successor value but forgetting to remove the successor node
